claim: Niconico Douga's paid-membership base peaked at 2.56 million in 2016 and fell by more than 1 million subscribers by 2021.
quoted_support: 2016年には主な収益源である有料会員が256万にまで達していた。しかし、翌2017年には常に拡大を続けてきた有料会員数が減少に転じており...2021年までに100万以上も減少している。 (In 2016, paid members -- the main revenue source -- reached 2.56 million. But in 2017, the paid-member count, which had continuously grown, turned to decline...by 2021 it had fallen by over 1 million.)

claim: Using Niconico's own quarterly video-post-count and view-count telemetry (2007 Q2-2021 Q2), video-posting-count began declining around 2011, roughly five years before total view-count began declining in 2016, indicating creator outflow preceded and likely caused viewer outflow rather than the reverse.
stance_target: income/monetization shortfall as a driver of platform-level creator exodus
scope_conditions: Japan, Niconico Douga, gaming video content category, 2007-2021
quoted_support: 動画投稿数の減少と再生数の減少には時差が生じており...動画投稿数の漸減≒段階的なクリエイターの流出が、即再生数減として現れたわけではないということであり、クリエイターの流出開始から視聴者の流出までは時差があったと言える。 (There is a time lag between the decline in video-posting count and the decline in view count...the gradual decline in posting count -- i.e. the gradual outflow of creators -- did not immediately appear as a decline in view count; there was a lag between the start of creator outflow and the start of viewer outflow.)

claim: The authors attribute Niconico's platform-level creator outflow to insufficient revenue-sharing: its 2011 'Creator Incentive Program' failed to produce a YouTube-Partner-Program-scale top earner (no creator reaching HIKAKIN-level income emerged), which the paper identifies as the primary reason gaming-video creators migrated to YouTube once YouTuber careers gained visibility from 2014.
stance_target: income level as a causal driver of creator platform-switching/exit
scope_conditions: Japan, Niconico vs YouTube, gaming-video-content creators, 2011-2021
quoted_support: 2011年に...ニコニコ動画が開始した「クリエイター奨励プログラム」だが...HIKAKIN氏に代表されるような大きな収益を得るクリエイターを生み出せていない。当然、YouTuberという存在が2014年頃から大きく話題になると、クリエイターがより稼げる可能性のあるYouTube等に移行しようとするのは必然であると考えられる。 (The 'Creator Incentive Program' Niconico launched in 2011...failed to produce creators earning large income like HIKAKIN. Naturally, once 'YouTuber' became a major topic around 2014, it was inevitable that creators would migrate to YouTube, where they could potentially earn more.)
numbers: YouTube Partner Program opened to general users April 2011

claim: In an original Dynata-fielded survey of Japanese gaming-video viewers (screening n=3,328; main survey of lapsed Niconico viewers n=1,356, stratified by sex x age-decade 10s/20s/30s, fielded Aug 24-Sep 7 2021), 'creators/streamers moved to other services' was the top or joint-top reason for quitting Niconico viewership in every one of six demographic cells, ranging from 29% to 42%.
stance_target: creator outflow as the leading viewer-perceived cause of platform decline
scope_conditions: Japan, ages 10s-30s, gaming-video/live-stream viewers, survey fielded Aug-Sep 2021
quoted_support: 全性年代で理由として挙げられているのは、「投稿者・配信者の他サービスへの移動」...であり、ニコニコ動画の問題としてあげた点と合致する。 (Across all sex/age groups, the reason cited was 'creators/streamers moving to other services'...consistent with the problems already identified for Niconico.)

claim: This is a platform-level aggregate telemetry study (quarterly posting/view-count time series as a population-level creator-outflow proxy), not an individual-creator cohort survival curve or hazard model, and its reason data surveys viewers about why they stopped watching, not creators about why they stopped creating.
stance_target: limits of what this source can establish about creator-level survival telemetry
quoted_support: 本研究では、ニコニコ動画からのゲーム実況ユーザーの流出要因の分析を通して、ゲーム動画コンテンツ市場におけるプラットフォーム間競争を考察する。 (This study considers inter-platform competition in the gaming video content market through an analysis of the factors behind the outflow of gaming-live-commentary users from Niconico.)
